items.action: Look at every screen with a ds-stat whose value is longer than its tile, and decide per tile whether the clipped value is acceptable or the value should wrap.
items.appliesWhen: Any ds-stat, and only where the label or value is wider than the card. A tile whose value fits renders identically and needs nothing. Tiles that already set --ds-stat-value-white-space are unaffected in shape — they wrapped before and wrap now.
items.pitfall: Nothing fails to build and nothing is lost to a screen reader, so this only shows on the screen: a tile that read in full because its value painted over the neighbouring card now ends in an ellipsis, and the text is reachable only by hovering or focusing it.
items.verify: No ds-stat value paints outside its own card at any viewport width, and every tile whose value is clipped opens a tooltip carrying the full value on hover.
items.note: The value carried `white-space: nowrap` and no overflow rule, so a phrase ran past the card and over its neighbour — 158px past a 240px tile at the default size. It now takes the same single-line ellipsis the other eleven text-bearing components use. The restore snippet keeps every character visible by wrapping, which grows the tile instead; there is no hook that brings back the value escaping the card, because that was the defect. Three hooks shape it and they compose: `white-space`, `--ds-stat-value-lines` for the ellipsis on line N, and `--ds-stat-value-wrap: anywhere` for a word wider than the tile (delete list: stat-wrap-hook-for-spill).

items.action: Replace any flow or test that clicked a truncated cell, or read its `title`, with one that hovers or focuses it and reads the tooltip.
items.appliesWhen: Only where a column sets `truncate`. A table without truncated columns never rendered the popover and sets no `title`, so nothing changes for it.
items.pitfall: An end-to-end test that asserted `title` on `.cell-clip` now reads null and a click on the cell opens nothing — both pass as "no error" while the assertion silently stops testing disclosure.
items.verify: Hovering a truncated cell shows the full value, and a cell that already reads in full shows nothing.
items.note: The cell set `title` on every truncated cell and opened a popover on click; the header set `title` from its own pointer-enter handler. All three are `dsTooltipWhenClipped` now, which fires on hover and on focus and stays shut when the text already fits — so the disclosure reaches the keyboard, which the click popover never did. `title` is dropped deliberately: together with a tooltip it renders the same text twice, once styled and once by the OS (delete list: table-cell-text-pop-styling).

items.action: Rename your subclass member where it collides, or add `override` where the base member genuinely matches; drop an override of a member that no longer exists on the base.
items.appliesWhen: Only a class that extends one of the two named below. Subclassing a DS component is unsupported (design-system.md § Components), so most consumers are unaffected.
items.pitfall: A gained name fails the build loudly (TS4114 / TS2416), but a LOST one does not: an `override` of a member the base no longer declares is an error, while a method that merely shadowed one now runs as your own code with nothing calling it.
items.verify: The consumer app type-checks, and no subclass declares `override` on a member the base no longer has.
items.note: TooltipDirective gained `dsTooltipWhenClipped` and `tipText`; ButtonComponent gained the five destination modifiers plus `routerLinkActiveOptions`, `ariaCurrent` and two resolvers; SidenavItemComponent and SidenavGroupComponent each gained `ariaCurrent` and two resolvers. TableComponent lost `cellPopoverText`, `isClipped`, `onCellClipClick` and `onHeaderEnter` — the three hand-rolled disclosures it carried, now one directive. The compiler enumerates every collision on the first build, which is why the names live here and not in the action.

items.action: Rename the token where you set it.
items.appliesWhen: Only a stylesheet that sets `--ds-button-border`. `--ds-button-border-width` is a different token and is NOT renamed — check the word boundary before replacing.
items.pitfall: A blind replace of `--ds-button-border` also rewrites `--ds-button-border-width` into `--ds-button-border-color-width`, which resolves to nothing and drops the declaration.
items.verify: No stylesheet names `--ds-button-border` without the `-color` or `-width` suffix.
items.note: The token sets the border COLOUR, and since the width moved out to `--ds-button-border-width` the bare name read as a `border` shorthand. Rename the longer `--ds-button-border-disabled` first — it is a separate entry, and the shorter name is a prefix of it.

items.action: Rename the token where you set it.
items.note: Same correction as the resting colour beside it. Rename this one FIRST: the shorter `--ds-button-border` is a prefix of it, so the other entry run first would corrupt this name.

items.action: Update any assertion that expected `aria-current="page"` on a link whose destination is a PREFIX of the current URL — it reads `true` now.
items.appliesWhen: Only a `routerLink` destination on `ds-button`, `ds-sidenav-item` or `ds-sidenav-group`, and only where the destination is an ancestor of the current URL. An exact destination still announces `page`. Nothing changes on screen: the `active` class still matches by prefix.
items.pitfall: Nothing renders differently, so a screen is no evidence either way — the only readers are a screen reader and a test that reads the attribute.
items.verify: A link whose destination IS the current URL announces `page`; a link to a section the reader is inside announces `true`; every other link announces nothing.
items.note: `aria-current` was derived from `routerLinkActive`, which matches by prefix, so a back-link claimed to be the page the reader was leaving. ARIA separates them: `page` is the page you are on, `true` is the current section or an ancestor. `ariaCurrent` overrides the result where a link is a step or a location rather than a page, and `null` silences it.

items.action: Handle `UrlTree` where you read a `routerLink` value back off one of these components, or override the input in a subclass.
items.appliesWhen: Only code that READS or OVERRIDES `routerLink` on `ds-button`, `ds-sidenav-item` or `ds-sidenav-group`. Writing it is unaffected — every value that worked before still works.
items.pitfall: A widened union is source-compatible for whoever writes the value and breaking for whoever reads it back, so a consumer feels this only in a type error far from the binding — `link.split('/')` on a value that may now be a `UrlTree`.
items.verify: The consumer app type-checks with no cast added at a routerLink read.
items.note: `string | readonly unknown[] | null` became `DsRouterLink`, which adds `UrlTree`. It is what makes `relativeTo` and `preserveFragment` reachable without an input each. A subclass overriding the input breaks on the invariant `equal` position of `InputSignalWithTransform` even where the values are compatible.

items.action: Re-point any rule that styles the group’s box at `ds-field-group .row`, or replace it with the matching `--ds-field-group-*` token.
items.appliesWhen: Only a stylesheet that reaches `ds-field-group` itself to change the border, radius, padding, background or overflow. Overrides written through `--ds-field-group-*` tokens need nothing — the tokens are still declared on the host. Layout properties on the host (width, margin, display) are unaffected.
items.pitfall: The rule still matches an element, so nothing errors and the selector does not go red in a linter — it simply styles a box that no longer draws the border.
items.verify: The group renders with your border/radius as before, and the message row sits outside the bordered box.
items.note: The group carries its own message row now, and that line has to sit outside the border — so the host became the column that stacks the two and `.row` became the bordered box. A group with no message keeps the same outer box it had: measured at 40px row and 40px host, growing to 57px only once `error` or `hint` is bound.

informational: `ds-button` takes five more style hooks — `--ds-button-font-family`, `--ds-button-line-height`, `--ds-button-border-width`, `--ds-button-label-color-hover` and `--ds-button-label-color-active`. Every one defaults to the value the stylesheet read before it, so nothing moves for a button that sets none of them. Worth knowing if you reached the same values the hard way: `ds-button { --font-sans: … }` and a subtree override of `--border-width-default` both have a hook of their own now, and neither of those workarounds stops working.

`ds-stat` takes two more hooks beside the existing `--ds-stat-value-white-space`: `--ds-stat-value-lines` puts the ellipsis on the line you name once the value wraps, and `--ds-stat-value-wrap: anywhere` breaks a word wider than the tile. Both default to the shape the component already had, so a tile that sets neither is unaffected by them.

`dsTooltipWhenClipped` is public on the tooltip directive: the tip opens only while its host is showing less text than it holds, and with no `dsTooltip` text it discloses the host's own text. `isTextClipped(element)` from `/core` is the same test on its own — horizontal only, descendants included. Additive; an existing `[dsTooltip]` binding behaves exactly as before.

`ds-button` forwards `fragment`, `queryParams`, `queryParamsHandling`, `target` and `rel` to the anchor it renders, and `routerLink` on it, `ds-sidenav-item` and `ds-sidenav-group` now also accepts a `UrlTree` for the options with no input of their own. All additive. If you kept a hand-written button class for controls that needed one of these, it can go (delete list: hand-written-button-class-for-modifiers).

`routerLinkActiveOptions` and `ariaCurrent` are public on the same three components — the first moves what the `active` class matches, the second overrides what the link announces. Neither is needed for the corrected default.

`ds-field-group` takes `error`, `hint` and `warning` — the same message inputs every field takes, resolved by the same code. `error` turns the state on and carries the text; `invalid` stays the flag for when the text lives in a form-level summary. Every segment gains `aria-invalid` while the group is in error and points at the one message through `aria-describedby`. Additive: a group binding neither renders exactly as before.
